**Title:** *Evening Tide, the Estuary*

It's a Thames-style sailing barge with russet sails, dark against the gold light just after sunset. A mauve bank of cloud crosses the sky, and a low cool shore holds a clump of trees, a windmill and one far-off sail. The barge's reflection is broken into ripples. A dark mud spit with mooring stakes and marsh grass anchors the lower left. The water is calm and gold near the horizon and gets darker and choppier towards the viewer.

The painting took a lot of correcting. One blend dragged the foresail into the sky, a glaze meant to be thin went on almost black, and a sheen on the mud turned into a pale mound. Each time I let the paint dry and painted over it, since nothing can be undone. Some of those accidents stayed: the dark glaze became the wind-ruffled foreground water.

In the last session I:
- darkened the reflection under the hull
- dulled the puddles on the mud
- broke up the mast's reflection
- added four gulls
- glazed the top of the sky and the lower-right water to keep the eye inside the picture

The top glaze came out streaky. After one soft blend I kept it as windblown cloud.

- **Title:** *Barge at Slack Water, Evening*

It's a Thames-style sailing barge with tan sails, set dark against a low estuary sky just after sunset. The glow lies in a band of pale gold along the horizon. Above it a mauve-grey cloud bank crosses the sky, and a streak of cloud at the top was left the way the glaze fell. On the far shore there's a low line of tree clumps, a windmill and a small distant sail, which balance the barge across the empty right half. The barge's reflection is broken into horizontal dashes on the water. In the foreground a dark mud spit with mooring posts and marsh grass anchors the lower left.

In this last session, the mainsail still looked flat, like a cut-out. I added a narrow broken edge of warm light along the outer edge of the mainsail and the head of the topsail, so the evening light seems to come through the cloth from behind. Some of that paint landed along the bottom of the sail as a pale patch, and I covered it with the deep sail colour. I left the rest as it was, because more work would only have muddied it.

- **Title:** *Slack Water, Evening*

A Thames-style sailing barge with russet sails stands dark against a low gold sky just after sunset. Its reflection breaks up in the water beneath it. The far shore is a thin cool strip with a windmill, a small distant sail and a clump of trees. A dark mud spit with old mooring posts holds the lower left corner. The picture works mostly through value: the bright band on the horizon, the dark shape of the barge, and the heavier dark of the foreground.

This time I changed only one thing. The two puddles on the mud were still bright cream shapes that looked cut out, and they pulled the eye away from the barge. Once the paint was dry, I glazed them with a thin cool mauve so they reflect the same sky as the estuary. Then I added a faint gold line along the far edge of each for the glow on the horizon. I left everything else alone.

The picture is an estuary just after sunset, oil on linen, 600 × 400 mm. A Thames-style sailing barge with tan sails stands dark against a low gold sky. Its reflection breaks up in the water beneath it. The far shore is a thin cool strip with a clump of trees, a small windmill and one distant sail, which balance the barge across the empty right half. A muddy marsh spit with mooring posts anchors the lower left. The sky takes up about two thirds of the height and cools from the gold at the horizon through mauve cloud to grey-blue at the top.

The sails are painted almost flat, as silhouettes against the light. Only a narrow warm edge along the right side of the mainsail (the leech) suggests the glow coming through the cloth.

This last time I painted nothing. I looked at the canvas whole, close up and in the value and squint views, and it holds up. Working it again would only muddy it.
